title: Comment register and lint
overseerSummary: Zero behaviour change. Low priority; it touches 21 files, so it runs alone at the end of wave 1.

proposals.title: Comments in the engineering register, with a lint test that keeps them there
proposals.problem: Code comments in game-owned files still use the register the user has rejected twice: shouted maxim lead-ins, personification and aphorism. One comment contains the exact sentence the memory file quotes as a banned example, and four comments state something the code contradicts or use class names that no longer exist.
evidence: Lead-ins of 15 or more capitals followed by a full stop or colon: 66 in 20 files outside facet/, generator and vendor (field.js 16, potential.js 6, game.js 4, then temper, sortie, quests, missiontypes, combat, classes, bonds with 3 each). Examples: field.js:1582 'A HARDCORE CONTRACT HAS A CLOCK EVEN WHEN ITS TYPE DOES NOT.', field.js:1594 'THE PAPER DOES NOT CARE HOW IT FELT.', sortie.js:427 'WHAT HOLDING ON IS WORTH.', missiontypes.js:985 'THE CLOCK NO LONGER KILLS ANYBODY.', game.js:1643 'NOTHING DRAINS GEMS.'

grep -n -i -E 'whole point|is the point|not a detail|a promise|silently|quietly' over game-owned .js and .html (excluding facet/ and generator): 35 matches in 18 files (field 6, game 5, crew 4, sacrifice 3). Not every match is wrong; each needs reading.

combat.js:34-37: 'a mortality bound that silently does nothing is a promise this code has made to the player and broken', the sentence quoted as banned in ui-prose-engineer-style.md; its stated replacement is 'Facet.install throws instead of warning, because a silent failure here disables the damage bound'.

crew.js:322 header says '2. GEMS maintenance, sized to what a town this big and this tall costs to keep'; crew.js:383 says 'this one is INCOME rather than a bill. Nothing drains gems on a tick' and game.js:1643-1645 says 'NOTHING DRAINS GEMS'; numbers-must-be-traceable.md names the bill wording as the trap.

condition.js:24-27 says 'Nothing here reaches into a fight: combat.js has its own per-encounter pools and always did'; combat.js:80-88 reads co.staminaFrac(c) and co.poolFrac(c) when it builds a fighter's pools.
psionic.js:212 'a Temporizer has speed and clairvoyance' (the class is chronokinetic since classes.js LEGACY_IDS); classes.js:1105 doc example 'an Adept Killer' (the class is butcher).
proposals.change:
1) Rewrite the four contradicting or stale comments: combat.js:34-37 to 'Facet.install throws instead of warning, because a silent failure here disables the damage bound'; crew.js:322 to 'GEMS income target (a savings rate; nothing drains gems)'; condition.js:24-27 to say combat.js reads staminaFrac and poolFrac when it builds a fighter's pools; psionic.js:212 and classes.js:1105 use current class names.
2) Replace each of the 66 shouted lead-ins with a plain topic sentence that states the mechanism and keeps every fact that followed (for example field.js:1594 becomes 'Terms are read before the withdrawal flag: a squad that withdrew but met the terms has completed the job'). No code line changes.
3) Read each of the 35 pattern matches and rewrite those that are metaphor or aphorism; keep the ones that describe a real silent failure.
4) New test/register.js (Node): fails on a comment line in game-owned .js files that matches a lead-in of 15 or more capitals or one of the six phrases above, with an allowlist for facet/, vendor/, test/ and generator files; prints file:line.
5) Edit one file at a time, re-reading the file immediately before each edit because another session edits this folder. Do not touch facet/*.js (pinned by facet/MANIFEST.json).
proposals.playerEffect: No change in play. Whoever reads or extends the code finds the same register as the class text, and the lint test stops it from drifting back.
proposals.secondOrder: The lint test gives later builders an immediate failure instead of a review comment. Comments that now say how combat reads fatigue and what crew gems mean agree with the code and with the UI.
proposals.risks: Comment-only edits carry no behaviour risk, but 20 files overlap other builders' edits; apply at the end of the round, or per file immediately after its owner finishes. A careless rewrite could drop a fact from a comment; the rule is to keep every fact.
proposals.response: Split out of cleanup-register-pass as the engineering attacker demanded: this part ships with zero behaviour change. Design demand to fix condition.js:24-27 (a contradiction the first pass missed): verified against combat.js:80-88 and added. The pattern counts are re-measured today: 35 matches in 18 files for the phrase list (not 28 in 13, because files changed and generator is excluded) and 66 shouted lead-ins, which the first pass did not count and which are the larger share of the problem.
